newsitem.title: USA: CBOT March oats collapse amid delivery rumor.
newsitem.headline: CBOT March oats collapse amid delivery rumor.

text.p: CBOT March oat futures dropped sharply on rumors that commercials would deliver a large amount of oats on that contract, traders said.
"Rumors circulated commercials will deliver and with this kind of spread I don't blame them," a trader said.
The March/May spread closed at roughly 16 cents per bushel, premium March a three cent narrowing from the 19 cent spread posted at Thursday's close.
Oats surged early this week on percptions for light deliveries on the March as the Canadian transportation snarl could slow oat shipments into the U.S.
But traders pointed out there were 3.180 million bushels of oats in Minneapolis registered for potential delivery on the CBOT oat contracts.
First notice day for delivery on the CBOT March contracts is slated for Feb 28.
The July and far deferred months gained on spreads with the nearbys on prospects for light oat seedings this year in the U.S.

Grain experts Friday said the possibility of planting delays in the northern U.S. Plains and the relative attractiveness of competing cash crops could further shrink U.S. oat acreage and output in 1997.
Oat futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 2,000 contracts, below Thursday's tally of 3,277.
Oat futures closed 8-1/2 cents lower to one cent higher, with March down 8-1/2 at $1.72-1/4 a bushel, May down 5-1/4 at $1.56-1/2 and July 1-3/4 lower at $1.56.
